content: Now here's the real reason I need WordLand and if you write for WordPress sites, I think you'll want it too. It's because WordPress is like the Microsoft Word of web writing. If you ask someone how they do their site, it's probably going to be WordPress in 2025. So if someone invites you to write a guest post on their blog, chances are pretty good I can write it in WordLand, and it'll be archived there, and easy for me to find, because that's what it does for writers. So I was able to create the new post on the WordCamp site in less than a minute, and it was completely painless. And that's the point.
